differences.difference: The wrong choice claims the ball is slower on the way up in English but only that it moves slowly on the way up in Sinhala. The stated comparison is lost.
The Sinhala keyed choice explicitly says forward friction. The English choice names ground friction on the foot and leaves its direction to the student.
Sinhala names the driven tyres and tells the student the friction points forward. English asks the student to infer this from road friction on the tyres.
The diver spins faster after tucking in English. Sinhala says the diver spins fast and leaves the change from the earlier speed unstated.
English tests whether increasing spin speed increases inertia. Sinhala asks about spinning fast, without saying the spin speed increased.
Sinhala specifies a vertical launch. English says upward, which also allows an oblique launch. The keyed u²/(2g) needs u to be the vertical component.
English explicitly assumes still air as well as negligible drag. Sinhala asks the reader to ignore air resistance and leaves air motion unspecified. Both give the same flight-time result.
English launches the ball from the ground. Sinhala gives the angle and speed but leaves the starting height open. The requested speed is unaffected.
English makes the claim for every ball. Sinhala extends it to every object. Both claims are false in the projectile model.
English specifies downward acceleration. Sinhala describes downward travel with acceleration a. A descending lift that is slowing down has upward acceleration and a different scale reading.
English asks how much truck acceleration the friction can give the box. Sinhala asks only for the maximum box acceleration. The values coincide at the no-slip limit.
English changes the speed of the same disc. Sinhala says it is spun fast. An absolute speed replaces the comparison in the false claim.
English compares lighter molecules with heavier ones. Sinhala says lighter molecules move fast without saying faster than the heavier ones.
English says cooling slows as the body approaches room temperature. Sinhala describes slow cooling near room temperature without explicitly comparing the rates.
The distractor says cooling is faster at lower temperatures. Sinhala says it is fast there, losing the comparison.
Sinhala explicitly puts the two phases in equilibrium. English only says they coexist. Equilibrium makes the constant melting-temperature argument explicit.
English mixes two samples of air. Sinhala says gas samples without specifying air. The vapour-mass calculation still uses the stated total volume.
English fixes the air temperature. Sinhala fixes the gas temperature without identifying the gas as air. The humidity relation is otherwise the same.
English gives the real meter a similar resistance. Sinhala can be read as equal resistance. That is a narrower loading condition, although the reading falls in either case.
English says drift must be faster through the smaller area. Sinhala says fast drift is necessary. The requirement is relative, not an absolute speed.
English claims a faster reading than the alternative instrument. Sinhala says the reading is quick. Neither wording is the keyed advantage.
English says back e.m.f. grows as the coil turns faster. Sinhala says it grows when the coil turns fast. A constant high speed gives constant back e.m.f.
English gives another, different cell. Sinhala specifies that its e.m.f. differs. Two distinct cells could have the same e.m.f. in the English setup.
English says electrons drift faster in the thin section than in the thick section. Sinhala just says they drift fast. Even the faster drift speed can be very small.
The false statement says electrons drift more slowly in the thin section. Sinhala says they drift slowly, which can be true in both sections.
The explanation repeats the missing comparison. It describes fast drift at small area without saying faster than at large area.
English calls the connection a tap. Sinhala calls it the midpoint. This is a junction of unequal resistors, so it need not be halfway in potential.

English names the conductance of the cell combination, measured in siemens. Sinhala uses සන්නායකතාව, also the textbook term for material conductivity, measured in siemens per metre. Specify the reciprocal of the combination’s resistance.
English leaves “across it” ambiguous between the meter and resistor. Sinhala names the resistor. Both versions still describe the wrong function for an ammeter.
